turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Come on in and sit yourself down, Mrs Kearney. How are you keeping?
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Ah, not the best, doctor. I'm after having the runs, and I was getting sick as well.
[SEG0003] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'm sorry to hear that. Tell me a bit about it, in your own time.
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): Well, we were down for my niece's wedding. The dress was gorgeous, I'll say that, but the hotel dinner and all, and then this started on me.
[SEG0005] person_3 (CAREGIVER): I'm Nuala, her carer. I was with her the whole weekend. The reception was Saturday, lovely band, hotel out in Galway.
[SEG0006] person_1 (DOCTOR): Grand. When did the diarrhoea actually start, would you say?
[SEG0007] person_2 (PATIENT): Um, I don't know, doctor. Two days, I'd say? Or maybe it was Sunday. I'm all mixed up.
[SEG0008] person_3 (CAREGIVER): It was Saturday night, a few hours after the meal. That's three days now, not two. She's losing track of it.
[SEG0009] person_1 (DOCTOR): Right so. And the vomiting, is that still going on?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): No, that's stopped. I haven't got sick since yesterday evening.
[SEG0011] person_3 (CAREGIVER): She did, doctor. She vomited this morning in the bathroom. I had to clean it up.
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): I don't think that was this morning. I don't know, maybe I'm wrong, but I don't remember it.
[SEG0013] person_1 (DOCTOR): Okay. How many times have you been to the toilet with the diarrhoea?
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): I don't know, doctor. A good few. Six, or eight? I lose count once I'm going all the time.
[SEG0015] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Nearer ten, I'd say, since yesterday morning. Watery, every time.
[SEG0016] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any blood in it, or anything black?
[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Nothing like that. Just water, nearly.
[SEG0018] person_1 (DOCTOR): And the tummy itself, is there pain?
[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): Cramps, low down. They come on fierce before I have to run, and they ease a small bit after.
[SEG0020] person_1 (DOCTOR): Are you managing to drink at all?
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): A small bit of water. I'm thirsty the whole time. I don't know if it's enough, doctor.
[SEG0022] person_3 (CAREGIVER): And she's hardly passed urine. A small drop this morning, very dark, and nothing much since yesterday.
[SEG0023] person_1 (DOCTOR): Anyone else from the wedding taken bad?
[SEG0024] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Her sister, and two of the cousins. Texting this morning, the same thing, runs and getting sick. They all sat at our table.
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): I had the fish, though, not the chicken. I don't know if that even matters.
[SEG0026] person_1 (DOCTOR): It might not be the one plate, so, if the whole table is down with it. Any fever, or shivers?
[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): I don't think so. I feel a bit cold now and again, but I haven't a clue, really.
[SEG0028] person_3 (CAREGIVER): I took her temperature this morning before we came out. It was 36.8, normal.
[SEG0029] person_1 (DOCTOR): What medicines are you taking these days?
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): The blood pressure tablet, the little white one, every morning. And I've been taking the Imodium for the runs.
[SEG0031] person_1 (DOCTOR): Imodium is loperamide. How many of those have you had?
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): Um, I don't know, doctor. Maybe two after each time I go? Or, well, actually, was it one. The box said two to start. I'm not sure I did it right.
[SEG0033] person_3 (CAREGIVER): She's been taking them since Sunday, and the chemist told her not to, if it was a bug off the food. She took them anyway.
[SEG0034] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'd stop the Imodium now. If this is a tummy bug, better to let it out than cork it up.
[SEG0035] person_2 (PATIENT): Oh. I thought I was doing the right thing. Sorry, doctor.
[SEG0036] person_1 (DOCTOR): You're grand, no harm done yet. Do you know the name of the little white tablet?
[SEG0037] person_2 (PATIENT): I don't know, doctor. It's just the blood pressure one. I've been on it for years.
[SEG0038] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Ramipril, five milligrams, one every morning. She doesn't miss that one.
[SEG0039] person_1 (DOCTOR): Lovely, stay on the ramipril. Any water tablet, or anything for the sugar?
[SEG0040] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Just that, and the Imodium I was telling you about.
[SEG0041] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'll have a quick look at you now, if that's alright. Pulse, pressure, and your tummy.
[SEG0042] person_1 (DOCTOR): Pulse is 98, blood pressure 112 over 68, and the temperature here is 37.1.
[SEG0043] person_1 (DOCTOR): Your tongue is dry, and the skin on the back of your hand is a little slow coming back. Tummy is soft, tender low down, no guarding.
[SEG0044] person_2 (PATIENT): Is that serious, doctor? I don't know what any of that means.
[SEG0045] person_1 (DOCTOR): It's mild dehydration, that's all. Not severe. My first thought was to send a stool sample off today and maybe give you a tablet for the infection.
[SEG0046] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Would a sample not be the sensible thing, with so many of them sick?
[SEG0047] person_1 (DOCTOR): I was leaning that way, but actually, no. Others are ill the same way, there's no blood, and it's only a few days. I won't send a sample today.
[SEG0048] person_1 (DOCTOR): If it hasn't settled in three or four days, then we might send a stool off. No antibiotic either, I changed my mind on that. It should be a short food bug or a virus.
[SEG0049] person_2 (PATIENT): So what do I do, just wait? I don't know if I can face food.

[SEG0050] person_1 (DOCTOR): Sip Dioralyte, little and often, even a teaspoon every few minutes. Flat 7-Up if the Dioralyte turns your stomach. Plain food when you fancy it, nothing greasy, and leave the Imodium in the press.
[SEG0051] person_2 (PATIENT): I don't know if I'll keep the Dioralyte down, doctor.

[SEG0052] person_1 (DOCTOR): Tiny sips all the same. If you can't keep any fluid down, or you go dizzy, or you see blood, or the urine dries up completely, come straight back or go on to the emergency department.
[SEG0053] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Will you want to see her again this week?
[SEG0054] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'm not booking a routine visit. If you're not clearly better in three or four days, come back and we'll see about that stool test then.
[SEG0055] person_2 (PATIENT): Alright. I hope I'm not being a bother over nothing.
[SEG0056] person_1 (DOCTOR): Not a bit of it. Mind yourself, and Nuala will keep an eye. You'll likely turn the corner shortly.

features: doctor_misses_topics: the doctor does not ask about everything; topics never discussed are simply absent (no invented denials, no allergy line if allergies were never mentioned).

colloquial_drug_names: medicines referred to by colour, purpose or brand ('the water tablet', 'Crocin', 'my sugar tablets', 'the purple inhaler'); the name is recorded as said, the normalized name only if it is clear.
doctor_changes_mind: the doctor says one plan, then changes it after new information; the label holds the final plan.
hedged_plan: the doctor hedges ('we might do a scan if it does not settle', 'let's see in two weeks'). Conditional vs planned status must follow the words.

omissions.text: Diarrhoea frequency and character were described as about 6-8 by patient and nearer 10 since yesterday morning by caregiver, watery every time.
Vomiting was reported by the patient to have stopped since yesterday evening, with caregiver disputing this and stating she vomited this morning.
Reduced urine output detail: only a small amount of very dark urine this morning and little since yesterday.
Others from the wedding/table were also ill: her sister and two cousins had the same symptoms.
Negative finding asked and answered: no fever; caregiver reported temperature normal at home.
Medication detail omitted/wrongly incomplete: patient was taking Imodium/loperamide at an uncertain dose, possibly two after each episode of diarrhoea or one; box said two to start.
Negative medication history asked and answered: no water tablet and nothing for diabetes/sugar.
Doctor initially considered stool sample and an antibiotic, then explicitly changed plan: no stool sample today and no antibiotic.
Follow-up plan detail: no routine review booked.
